decision.why:
HELD OUT by user ruling 2026-08-02 (Issue #261 wave-2 packet, item 2c -- ADR-0102, the hand-size relief promotion). The ruling is ACCEPT: the DECISION is unchanged and correct, and what moved is the leaf's forced-first RANKING, which is the composition POC-T3 replaces.

WHAT MOVED. Discrimination Gate, `82522726|1|decision|7`, OK -> MISS, rank 1 -> 2.
  baseline leaf values [58.0, 58.0, 58.0, 58.0, 8.0]   correct [0], top_tie 4
  now                  [ 8.0,  8.0,  8.0, 58.0, 8.0]   correct [0], rank 2
The baseline OK was LENIENT -- a four-way tie at 58.0, so the leaf never discriminated this frame; it now ranks option [3] (Harlequin) uniquely top and the three indistinguishable attaches at 8.0.

THE DECISION DID NOT MOVE. The shipped Pilot still plays [0], the human's ruled option. The Decision Gate reports 0 unruled REGRESSION on this build.

CAUSE, MEASURED IN THE GATE'S OWN PROCESS (the leaf value is pilot-state dependent, so an isolated two-frame reproduction does not reproduce it):
  * neutralising `_hand_size_relief_tactical` (the new term)  -> both flips REMAIN
  * restoring `play-harlequin-vs-hand-size` (+25) alone       -> GATE: PASS
So the flip is the +25's deletion, and the promoted term is not involved. On this board the relief is exactly 0.00 and correctly so: the opponent's Alakazam line is an Abra, so shrinking their hand buys no survival.

THE MECHANISM. `_engine_leaf_value(obs, [i])` forces option i and re-runs `decide()` greedily to the end of the turn. Once the {W} Energy is attached, `attach-before-hand-shuffle` (-60) stops firing and Harlequin sits at tactical -21.60; the +25 lifted that to +3.40, so the rollout played it and the end board banked the readiness of a simulated, auto-resolved draw. Without the +25 the rollout ends the turn, so every line that does not FORCE the refresh first loses that draw -- which is what makes forcing it look best. `_develop_rollout_line` already refuses to rank a stream-riding line for exactly this reason; `leaf_lab.board_leaf_values` bypasses that veto by design (it is measuring the leaf, not the rung).

NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately. The refresh is declined because ADR-0101's v2 SHED prices the hand's keep-cost -- the hand holds a Mega Starmie ex. Restoring a flat to lift it over that signed oracle is the ADR-0063 failure verbatim ("a booster must SCALE the oracle, never ADD to it"), and re-fitting the SHED to satisfy one leaf ranking moves every keep-value site including the discard decider's 12/12. The honest reading is that the leaf and the option scorer are two opinions about one board.

OWNER: #262 (POC-T3, `state_value`) -- it owns exactly this, "replace the develop rollout's `_engine_leaf_value` composition". When one composed scalar scores both the forced-first ranking and the option, the disagreement cannot exist. Delete this owner then.

NOTE ON SCOPE. The Held-out Ledger is whole-frame by design (gates.held_out_frames: the leaf verdict is not per-lane), so this entry also holds the frame out of the DECISION gate, where it currently passes. That cost is recorded rather than hidden.
